title: BYO corpus record — github
description: A GitHub issue or pull request. Title -> title, content -> body markdown. `container` is the repo name.

content.description: The retrieval payload served verbatim as the body.

title.description: Document title (email subject / file name / issue title / page title).

repo.description: The repo this document belongs to, as the API's bare `name` -- `gateway`, not `acme/gateway`. The owner is a path segment of its own, supplied from the org this mock serves, and `full_name` is composed from the two; a value that carries the owner is served as `name` verbatim and appears in `full_name` twice. GitHub's own rule for a repository name is the constraint -- "must not exceed 100 characters, and can only contain ASCII letters, digits, and the characters `.`, `-`, and `_`" -- so a slash or a space is refused. The further limits GitHub enforces but does not publish (a name of `.` or `..`, a `.git` suffix) are not.

group.description: ACL group owning the repo (default: slug(container)); null means the container owns no group, so nothing is group-scoped to it.

author_name.description: The owner's display name as the corpus writes it, served as the document's owner (a name is not recoverable from an email address).

visibility.description: public = org-wide, group = the container's group, private = author only.

readers.description: Explicit reader principals. `user:<email>` / `group:<id>` / `org:<name>` state the type; unprefixed, an address is a user and anything else a group. Overrides visibility — and an EMPTY array means nobody may read the document (admin-only), not everybody.

subtype.description: Issue vs PR vs file (default: issue).

ref.description: subtype='file' only: which SNAPSHOT of `path` this row is — a commit sha, a branch, or any label the corpus chooses. A file is addressed by (repo, path), so several rows may state one path; `ref` is what tells two of them apart. Omitted, the row's `created` is the discriminator and the newest snapshot is the one served, so a corpus recording one edit per date needs no ref. State one when two snapshots share a `created`, or to name the change they came from.

state.description: The issue/pull state GitHub reports. A merge is `merged_at`, not a third state.

updated.description: updated_at (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Default: created + 1h.

closed_at.description: When the issue/PR was closed (epoch seconds or ISO 8601). Default: derived from state.

closed_by.description: Email of the user who closed the issue.

merged_by.description: PR only: email of the user who merged it.

milestone.description: Milestone title (emitted as a milestone object).

requested_reviewers.description: PR only: emails of requested reviewers.

changed_paths.description: PR only: paths of the files this pull changed, as `path` values of this repo's subtype='file' docs. Omit it and the changeset is chosen deterministically instead, which is well-formed but unrelated to what the pull is about. The hunks themselves are always synthesized from the file's own snapshot. A path matching no such doc is dropped from the changeset — the import reports it and `--dry-run` names it, but loads the record as written, since a corpus may legitimately be a slice of the repo.

items.description: A comment on the document (served via the vendor's comment API).

created_ts.description: Optional creation time (epoch seconds or ISO string).

path.description: PR only: makes this a line-anchored REVIEW comment (GET /pulls/{n}/comments) on that file, rather than a conversation comment (GET /issues/{n}/comments). Real GitHub keeps the two resources apart; `path` is how a corpus says which one it means.

line.description: Review comment only: the line in `path` it is anchored to. Omit for a file-level comment, as real GitHub allows.

diff_hunk.description: Review comment only: the hunk it is anchored to. Derived from the file's snapshot around `line` when omitted.

number.description: Issue/PR number as the corpus writes it. Stored and served verbatim. An omitted number is synthesized from the doc_id at serve time, and a provided one claims that number ahead of every synthesized one in the same repository — so a corpus need only write the numbers its documents actually cite. Ignored on subtype: file rows.
